summary: All three gradient ramp builders walk stop ratios wrongly. Ruffle (render/wgpu/src/mesh.rs CommonGradient::new) advances its record cursor at most ONE step per texel and pins alpha to 0 when last.ratio == next.ratio, so a run of k duplicate-ratio stops renders as k consecutive 1-pixel bands and the following segment starts k-1 texels later; ratios are never sorted, so a decreasing ratio pins alpha to 1.0. Ours emits ZERO rows for a duplicate and ZERO for a decreasing ratio, and the recompiler copy additionally emits 336 rows into a 256-row slot for gradient_nonsequential_ratios, breaking the 'exactly 256 rows per gradient' texture-row invariant. Proven by porting both algorithms to Python: the model reproduces CI's outlier counts EXACTLY (61440 and 6912) and predicts 1280 and 5120 after the fix, both under budget; the radial row is 95.8% ring pixels that the fix removes. Corpus audit over 2848 SWFs found duplicate/non-monotonic static gradient ratios in exactly 4 tests, all already failing - zero regression risk. Separate leg (do NOT bundle): at interpolation=linearRGB our static ramp differs from Ruffle's by up to 13 channels on every row because Ruffle quantises in LINEAR space and converts per-pixel in gradient.wgsl while swf.cpp::linearRgbLerp converts back to sRGB first; 13 is under every affected tolerance so it is not what is failing. Independent slot: YES (edits swf.cpp ~7110/7515, ~1500 lines from flattening leg C at 8653). Recommended pairing: P1+P4.
cost: one shared 25-line helper + 3 call sites; recompiler change => worktree cmake + --recompile

summary: DisplayObject.opaqueBackground is unimplemented on both VMs. Ruffle paints a solid rectangle over the object's bounds before drawing it: two green blocks in visual/opaque_background (231232 excess, 99% of expected ink missing), a blue square behind the red circle in avm2/displayobject_opaque_background (17004 excess, ink IoU 1.00 / ncolors 2:2 / 21.3% repainted). Both reproduced locally at CI's exact numbers. Both are tolerance 1 / max_outliers 0 but the content is flat-colour axis-aligned rectangles, so exactness is achievable (same class as the s9 focus-rect rider). Risk: the fill must be ordered and clipped exactly like Ruffle - painted in the object's own space, under its children, interacting with scrollRect.

AVM2 Graphics.beginGradientFill ignores null alphas/ratios and draws nothing (blank_render, 117600 excess, tolerance 5 / max_outliers 0, ncolors 1 vs 114). Test.as passes null for both arrays. Ruffle's build_gradient_records (core/src/avm2/globals/flash/display/graphics.rs) reduces length only by the arrays that are present, defaults alpha to 1.0 and generates evenly spaced ratios (i*255)/(length-1) = 0,63,127,191,255. ~10 lines. Confidence capped because the golden's toml comments it as generated from Flash Player, not Ruffle, and max_outliers is 0. Same file as P5 but a different function - self-localise.

LINESTYLE2 with HasFillFlag calls parseFillStyles(1) and keeps only fill[0].r/g/b/a, which for a gradient fill style are never populated - so a gradient-filled stroke becomes transparent black. Proven from the generated C of acid-gradient-2: draws.h declares gradient_data[256][4] (the gradient IS registered) while color_data[0] = {0,0,0,0}. Ruffle renders a gradient-filled ring; we render an empty stage (12555 excess, tolerance 1 / max_outliers 0, reproduced locally). The renderer already has line-gradient plumbing (action.c:28719 line_interpolation, used by AVM1 lineGradientStyle), so this is recompiler wiring, not new GPU work. Shares SWFRecomp/src/swf.cpp with P1 - combining P1+P4 into one recompiler slot is the recommended pairing.
cost: medium; recompiler + static line-gradient style path
